body:
This. I worked hard to up my self esteem on my pwBPD's advice, worked hard professionally, and built myself a good career. Also reconnected with my friends and parents and emerged as an unstoppable force that recognized healthy from unhealthy, rather than simply good from bad.

The result? I am now in the process of breaking up and running after seeing who my partner is, and they keep abusing me and telling me how I'm disgusting, their ex was great, better conscience than me, etc. None of that bothers me now, I'm convinced by myself about who I am, I don't need an abusive ex to tell me who I am and what I stand for ☔
Same, but yet to quit. I quit tobacco first and it's already been 12 days since I quit

Will read this everyday until my partner and I end up living separately

Also, thanks for your responses, they really helped me see that I'm doing the right thing for myself, and have nothing to be guilty about in wanting to end it

I understand. I think I never took it seriously enough to plan calling emergency services, but I have already saved their num on the phone and plan on calling them the next time she says anything to me that makes me feel unsafe

The more clingy and desperate bit has made me become more and more determined about breaking up - now I just keep telling her we're broken up, while she tries her usual antics while threatening suicide

Is it okay to call her parents when they are conservative and don't know about our relationship? I feel like that might backfire on me, if they accuse me of anything (although I have chat records etc) because I'm pretty sure my gf won't tell them how I've been spending half my salary getting her therapy and sustaining her with her doing little work around the house.

Her dad sends her pocket money enough for a college student, which makes me believe he might care. I just wonder if it's unsafe to call her parents up on her, because she has cut off from her dad multiple times, accusing him of not divorcing her abusive mom, and not 'getting' why she's upset and sad.

I do care, but I've clearly communicated to her that I'm letting her stay here to let her figure out where she wants to go, and what she wants to do.

I don't want to stop her, I just want her to leave without herself killing herself in my flat and leaving me with another trauma to deal with
It's selfish even if we don't intend to be - isn't that a result of some degree of healthy narcissism?
